text:
Marat Khusnutdinov hasn't scored since Oct. 24, but the Bruins keep winning around him, four straight after Sunday's 4-1 over Florida. He has 6 points in 18 games and has played between 12 and 16 minutes almost every night in a bottom-six role.

His finishing is right on schedule (3 goals on 2.78 expected), and Boston has scored about 2.2 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice. The on-ice share is where we'd hesitate: the Bruins take 50% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him at five on five and are about four points better without him.

Evolving-Hockey liked him a lot last season: 1.6 wins above replacement, 79th among 401 forwards, mostly from even-strength offense. That suggests more than six points is in there. He's 24, a 2020 second-round pick of Minnesota who came to Boston in a trade, and his burst speed ranks in the 91st percentile. His shot doesn't (8th percentile), so he has to get close. We project about 13 goals and 33 points.
headline: Khusnutdinov fits the winning streak
